newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Preussen, Fluor sign on Lithuania terminal.
newsitem.headline: Preussen, Fluor sign on Lithuania terminal.

text.p: Germany's Preussen and U.S. group Fluor Daniels have signed a letter of intent to complete the construction of the Butinge oil terminal in Lithuania, a Butinge company official said on Monday.
The letter was signed at the weekend for the project, the cost of which has been estimated at about $200 million.
"The letters of intent cover all the phases of construction, including the pipelines, with the exception of one small sub-station," the official told Reuters.
"The project should be completed by September 1998."
The contracts have to be confirmed by the Lithuanian government and it is hoped the final signing will take place in mid-October at Fluor's Houston headquarters, he said.
The terminal has been much delayed due to funding problems, but new life was breathed into it in August when the government renegotiated an $80 million loan from the U.S. EXIM Bank.

Preussen is to build the main terminal, lay a pipeline to the Mazheikiai refinery and lay a pipeline on the seabed from the terminal to a pier about 10 km offshore. Fluor will construct the pier itself.
Butinge and Mazheikiai were recently merged with other state oil firms into a new holding company, Lithuanian Oil.
